paras: A faulty washing machine can bring your household routine to a standstill. Towels begin to pile up, school uniforms go unwashed, and a simple household task becomes an ongoing inconvenience.

Back In Action Appliance Repairs provides specialised **washing machine repairs in Melbourne** for front-loading and top-loading machines. Whether your washing machine will not drain, spin, fill, start, or complete a cycle, we will inspect the appliance and identify the underlying fault.

Every appointment begins with a careful diagnosis. We explain what we find in plain English and provide a fixed-price quote before beginning the approved repair. If replacing the washing machine would be more practical, we will give you an honest recommendation.

faults.title: Washing Machine Problems We Diagnose and Repair
items: Washing Machine Not Draining
A washing machine that will not drain may have a blocked filter, restricted hose, faulty drain pump, or another problem affecting the drainage system.
We inspect the relevant components to determine why water is remaining inside the drum. Once the fault has been identified, we explain the recommended repair and provide a fixed-price quote.
Washing Machine Not Spinning
Spin problems may be connected to an unbalanced load, worn drive component, motor fault, speed sensor issue, door lock problem, or another internal failure.
We test the machine to identify the cause rather than relying only on the visible symptom. This gives you a clearer understanding of what needs attention.
Washing Machine Leaking Water
Water may escape from the door seal, inlet hose, drain hose, pump, detergent dispenser, tub, or an internal connection.
Turn the washing machine off and stop using it if you notice a significant leak. Our technician can examine the appliance, locate the source, and recommend an appropriate solution.
Washing Machine Making Loud Noises
Banging, grinding, scraping, or squealing noises may indicate problems with the drum bearings, suspension system, shock absorbers, pump, motor, or an object trapped inside the machine.
The type of noise and the point in the cycle when it occurs can provide useful diagnostic information. Tell us what you hear when booking your appointment.
Washing Machine Door Will Not Open or Lock
A washing machine door may remain locked when water has not drained correctly or when the door interlock, handle, sensor, or control system has developed a fault.
Avoid forcing the door open, as this may damage the lock, handle, or surrounding components. We can diagnose the cause and explain the safest repair option.
Washing Machine Not Filling or Starting
If the washing machine will not fill or start, there may be an issue with the water supply, inlet valve, door lock, power connection, control system, or another electrical component.
We inspect and test the relevant systems to identify the underlying problem. If an error code is displayed, include it with your booking details.

advice.title: Is Your Washing Machine Worth Repairing?

Problems involving pumps, belts, door locks, inlet valves, hoses, and seals may often be resolved without replacing the machine. More extensive problems involving bearings, tubs, motors, or electronic control systems may require a closer comparison between repair costs and replacement value.

What washing machine problems can you repair?

Can you repair a washing machine displaying an error code?

Should I continue using my washing machine if it is leaking?

Why is my washing machine not draining or spinning?

A washing machine may stop draining because of a blocked filter, restricted hose, faulty pump, or control problem. A machine that will not spin may have an unbalanced load, door lock issue, worn drive component, motor fault, or sensor problem.
These symptoms may also be connected. If the machine cannot drain the water, it may not begin the spin cycle. A diagnostic assessment is the most reliable way to determine the cause.

Is it better to repair or replace my washing machine?

intro.title: Get Back to Warm, Dry Clothes Without the Wait
paras: A faulty dryer can leave damp washing hanging throughout your home and make it harder to keep up with everyday laundry. Whether the dryer has stopped heating, the drum will not turn, or each load takes several cycles to dry, a professional diagnosis can identify what is causing the problem.

Back In Action Appliance Repairs provides specialised **dryer repairs in Melbourne** for vented, condenser, and heat pump models. We diagnose faults affecting heating elements, thermal fuses, drive belts, rollers, sensors, motors, door switches, thermostats, and other essential components.

We also check the lint path and airflow because restricted ventilation can make a dryer work harder and contribute to overheating. Once we find the fault, we explain it in plain English and provide a fixed-price quote before approved work begins.

faults.title: Dryer Problems We Diagnose and Repair
items: Dryer Not Heating
A dryer that tumbles without producing heat may have a failed heating element, blown thermal fuse, faulty thermostat, sensor problem, or heat pump system fault.
We test the relevant components to determine why the dryer is not heating properly. After identifying the problem, we explain the required repair and provide a fixed-price quote.
Dryer Drum Not Turning
If the motor can be heard but the drum remains still, the dryer may have a snapped drive belt, worn idler pulley, failed motor, or problem with the drum support system.
We inspect the drive components and determine what is preventing the drum from turning. Avoid repeatedly starting the dryer, as continued operation may place additional strain on other components.
Dryer Taking Too Long to Dry Clothes
Long drying times may be caused by a blocked lint filter, restricted ducting, full condenser unit, damaged heating element, faulty moisture sensor, or airflow problem.
We assess the heating performance and airflow to find the underlying cause. Restoring efficient operation may help shorten drying times and reduce unnecessary strain on the appliance.
Dryer Making Squealing or Thumping Noises
Squealing, scraping, or thumping sounds may indicate worn drum rollers, bearings, glides, belts, or other moving components.
The type of sound and when it occurs can provide useful information about the fault. Tell us whether the noise happens continuously or only when the drum starts or changes direction.
Dryer Not Turning On
A dryer that does not start may have a faulty door switch, start switch, timer, control board, power connection, thermal fuse, or internal electrical problem.
We carry out diagnostic testing to identify the component affecting the dryer. If the appliance displays an error code, include the complete code when booking.
Dryer Overheating or Producing a Burning Smell

Overheating can be caused by lint build-up, restricted airflow, a failed cycling thermostat, or another internal fault. A burning smell may indicate that a component is overheating or starting to fail.

Stop using the dryer if it produces smoke, excessive heat, or a burning smell. Switch it off and disconnect it from the power supply if it is safe to do so, then arrange a professional assessment before using it again.

faults.title: Dishwasher Problems We Diagnose and Repair
items: Dishwasher Not Draining
Water left in the bottom of a dishwasher may be caused by a blocked filter, restricted drain hose, obstructed sump, faulty drain pump, or another drainage problem.

We inspect the drainage system to determine whether the problem can be resolved by clearing a blockage or whether a component requires repair or replacement. Avoid running another cycle if the dishwasher remains full of water or begins leaking.
Dishes Not Coming Out Clean
Poor cleaning results may be connected to blocked spray arms, dirty filters, low water pressure, a faulty wash pump, a failed diverter, or a detergent dispenser problem.

We assess the dishwasher's water supply, circulation, and spray performance to identify the cause. We can also advise whether loading practices, detergent selection, or routine maintenance may be affecting the result.
Dishwasher Not Drying
If dishes remain wet after the cycle, the dishwasher may have a failed heating element, faulty temperature sensor, rinse aid problem, or issue with the drying system.

Some modern dishwashers use condensation drying rather than exposed heating elements, so results can vary between models. We test the relevant components and explain whether the problem is mechanical or related to the selected program.
Dishwasher Leaking Water
Dishwasher leaks may come from a worn door seal, damaged hose, loose connection, cracked component, failed pump, excessive foaming, or overfill fault.
Stop using the dishwasher if water is escaping onto the floor or into surrounding cabinetry. Continued operation could cause further water damage or activate the appliance's flood protection system.
Dishwasher Not Filling With Water
A dishwasher that will not fill may have a restricted water supply, blocked inlet screen, faulty inlet valve, float switch problem, door latch fault, or activated flood protection system.
We test the water supply and relevant components to identify what is preventing the appliance from filling. If an error code appears, include the full code when booking your repair.
Dishwasher Not Starting or Displaying an Error Code

Starting problems may involve the door latch, control board, touch panel, power connection, sensor, or flood protection system. An error code can help identify which part of the dishwasher has detected a problem.
Record the complete code or take a clear photograph of the display before turning off the appliance. We will use this information as part of the diagnosis rather than relying on the code alone.
